on_screen_text: A turbofan: a giant fan driven by a jet engine at its core.
Two shafts, one inside the other, spinning at different speeds.
Suck: the fan pulls in a huge mass of air. most air bypasses the core, and makes most of the thrust.
Squeeze: stage after stage compresses the air about 40 times, heating it.
Bang: fuel burns continuously, hotter than the turbine metal's melting point.
The blades survive with cooling air and heat-resistant coatings. Blow: hot gas spins the turbines, then blasts out the back.
Suck, squeeze, bang, blow: all happening at once, continuously.

酷暑日 kokushobi - A day on which the high reaches 40C or more.

Clear narrative structure breaking down a complex meteorological topic (heatwaves, pressure systems, attribution) into digestible numbered sketchbook chapters.

Tasteful use of red hanko stamps and handwritten annotations to highlight key data points.

hook.first_3s: Dark navy background with large white and yellow outlined Chinese typography reading '导数: 如何描述“一瞬间”的变化？' (Derivative: How to describe change in an 'instant'?).
hook.why_it_grabs: Immediately presents a relatable real-world contradiction (how speedometers work vs. distance/time math formula) before the 3-second mark, forcing curiosity.

structure.audio: Voiceover introduces the problem of instantaneous speed where distance and time both approach zero.

structure.on_screen: Number line with accelerating car, function S = t^2 plotted on Cartesian plane, secant line AB with slope calculation
structure.audio: Explains average speed over an interval and connects it geometrically to the slope of a secant line.

structure.on_screen: Table shrinking time interval Δt from 1s down to 0.001s, average speed converging to 2, secant turning into tangent line
structure.audio: Demonstrates the limit process as Δt approaches 0 without ever actually dividing by zero.

structure.on_screen: Formal limit definition of derivative f'(x), breakdown of numerator and denominator, two-layer meaning (slope of tangent line & instantaneous rate of change)
structure.audio: Synthesizes the formal mathematical definition and its dual geometric/physical interpretations.

structure.on_screen: Step-by-step algebraic expansion of (x+h)^2 - x^2 over h, simplifying to 2x + h, then letting h -> 0 to get 2x
structure.audio: Walks through the algebraic derivation step by step.

structure.on_screen: Parabola on left with sliding tangent line showing slope, plotted as straight line y = 2x on right coordinate system
structure.audio: Shows how the derivative function maps every point on the original curve to its slope.

structure.on_screen: Cubic curve with animated dot moving along it, showing uphill (f'>0), peaks/valleys (f'=0), and downhill (f'<0)
structure.audio: Explains how derivatives act as a hiking trail gradient to find maximums, minimums, and inflection points.

structure.on_screen: Circular magnifying glass over parabola point (1,1) scaling up from 1x to 100x until the curve becomes a straight line; comparison with absolute value function y = |x|
structure.audio: Visual demonstration of local linearity and where derivatives fail at sharp corners.

structure.on_screen: Summary checklist of 4 key points, three thought-provoking homework questions, final sign-off
structure.audio: Summarizes key takeaways and leaves 3 conceptual questions for the viewer.
